content:
What's up with file#FieldTheory/AbsoluteGaloisGroup? There's one definition

/-- The absolute Galois group of `K`, defined as the Galois group of the field extension `K^al/K`,
  where `K^al` is an algebraic closure of `K`. -/
def absoluteGaloisGroup := AlgebraicClosure K ≃ₐ[K] AlgebraicClosure K

We set up some local notation G_K and then transfer the Group and TopologicalSpace instances from the galois group. This def should probably be an abbrev.

Next is

instance absoluteGaloisGroup.commutator_closure_isNormal :
    (commutator (G_K K)).topologicalClosure.Normal :=
  Subgroup.is_normal_topologicalClosure (commutator (G_K K))

which is just a wrapper around another theorem Subgroup.is_normal_topologicalClosure (which is named wrong and also should probably be an instance). This theorem abuses the defeq G_K K = Gal(AlgebraicClosure K/K) in order to have IsTopologicalGroup (G_K K).

Then there's a second definition, this one is properly an abbrev.

/-- The topological abelianization of `absoluteGaloisGroup`, that is, the quotient of
  `absoluteGaloisGroup` by the topological closure of its commutator subgroup. -/
abbrev absoluteGaloisGroupAbelianization := TopologicalAbelianization (G_K K)

This one also abuses defeq to get a IsTopologicalGroup (G_K K) instance. We set up some local notation G_K_ab for this one too.

That's the whole file. There's no API, nothing in mathlib imports this file, and it doesn't really prove any theorems either. What's the point of this file?
Added in #7783 by @María Inés de Frutos Fernández
I think we wouldn't mind deprecating this entire file. At most we should move the absoluteGaloisGroup abbrev elsewhere (though I'm not sure if it's even all that useful).
This file came from my Lean 3 formalization of the adele ring of a global field, where I used this in the statement of the main theorem of global class field theory.
It is used in FLT. Also I would suggest changing AlgebraicClosure to SeparableClosure.

Andrew Yang said:

It is used in FLT. Also I would suggest changing AlgebraicClosure to SeparableClosure.

IIRC there is an open PR by @Adam Topaz doing this.
#19616

Did I ever open that PR? I don't remember :)

But yes, please someone fix it.
Still, this should just be an abbrev, right? This file isn't actually proving anything new, just specializing results in other files.

It would be worthwhile to prove that the restriction Aut(Kˉ∣K)→Gal(Ks∣K)Aut(\bar K|K) \to Gal(K^s|K)Aut(Kˉ∣K)→Gal(Ks∣K) is an isomorphism of topoloical groups as part of this change. I don't think it's that hard to formalize.

I agree that would be good to have, but I think the current question of interest is whether we want to have absoluteGaloisGroup as a def or as an abbrev and whether it should be in the file that it is in.
The solution to missing API is definitely to add them instead of removing the def altogether.

Adam Topaz 发言道：

Did I ever open that PR? I don't remember :)

But yes, please someone fix it.

I remember there is some problem due to compactness? It is in mathlib about a year ago, so it should be able to work.
@Aaron Liu Why would you prefer it to be an abbrev? Is the general Galois setting missing some API that would allow to work on it without exposing its internal definition?
I would prefer AboluteGaloisGroup be an abbrev because it is missing all the API, there is no API for it.
of course, adding API and getting rid of the existing defeq abuse is another option
(also I just realized it's capitalized incorrectly as absoluteGaloisGroup)
So what's the plan on this currently?

so, there are two ways to define the absolute Galois group, right? as the Galois group of the separable, or the algebraic closure. so under that logic I guess it makes sense to make a def which encompasses both.
yes, those two are equivalent

If we have to chose in my opinion it should be the Galois group of the separable closure (= biggest galois extension). Then one can prove that it is also the automorphisms group of the algebraic closure.
